key_insight: Boundary geometry can change the optimal shallow ReLU approximation exponent even when dimension, error norm, and coefficient-weighting rule remain fixed.
engineering_relevance: For finite ReLU targets, the bounds yield compressed networks using only original neurons without increasing the weighted coefficient sum.
method: Incorporate domain geometry into weighted variation-space constraints.
Prove approximation upper and lower bounds using boundary-cap growth.
Identify optimal exponents and sharp weight thresholds for specified convex domains.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical bounds and optimality results for all planar convex bodies, their products with polytopes, and specified smooth convex bodies, rather than empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: Optimality guarantees depend on domain regularity and the error-norm range; coverage of every finite q ≥ 2 requires positive principal curvatures in the smooth-body results.
paper_title: Boundary Geometry Determines Optimal Shallow ReLU Approximation under Weighted Coefficient Constraints
